info.title: Hushscript Public API
info.description: The versioned, shape-frozen public surface of the Hushscript transcription API. Every route under /v1 republishes existing account behaviour in a contract that will not change underneath an integration; the equivalent unversioned /api routes back the Hushscript app itself and may change at any time. Authenticate with a session bearer token or a Personal Access Token in the Authorization header; a Personal Access Token additionally needs the scope named in each operation's x-required-scope extension, and the billing scope needs the account's machine-billing switch to be on as well. Every PAT-authenticated request, /v1 included, is throttled per token (1200 requests/60s); POST /v1/billing/setup-session and POST /v1/billing/purchase carry an additional, tighter per-account budget (60 requests/60s) ahead of the Stripe call they would otherwise make. A throttled request answers HTTP 429 rate_limited with a Retry-After header naming the wait in seconds; a well-behaved client should back off for that long before retrying.

get.summary: Read the account's balance, expiry and upload admission limits
get.description: Returns the caller's net credit balance, when that balance is next scheduled to expire without a completed transcription or purchase, whether a card is on file, the account's data region, and the account's current daily-minutes and concurrent-jobs limits. Call this before create_upload to confirm there is enough balance and daily headroom for the upload about to be attempted.

post.summary: Start a new transcription upload and place a credit hold
post.description: Declares the size and duration of a new audio upload, places a credit hold for the billable seconds (duration plus any transcription_options surcharge), and returns a job id plus, when direct-to-R2 uploads are available, a first page of presigned part URLs. Resending the same idempotency_key returns the already-created job instead of opening a second one. Long direct-to-R2 transfers must call heartbeat_upload periodically or the job is reaped as idle.

size_bytes.description: The exact declared byte size of the audio file, up to the 5 GB cap.

duration_seconds.description: The declared duration in seconds, from 15 seconds up to the 10 hour cap. Rechecked against the probed exact duration at complete_upload.

title.description: An optional display title. A value longer than 300 bytes is truncated on a character boundary rather than rejected, and this response does not echo the stored value; read it back from the transcript once the job completes. In `private` mode the title is not stored at all.

mode.description: Optional job mode, e.g. a private-result upload.

part_size_bytes.description: Optional smaller part size for a flaky connection. Clamped to this API's supported range; omit for the 32 MiB default.

idempotency_key.description: An optional client-minted key, 16 to 128 bytes. Resending the same key returns the same job with no second hold.

matter_code.description: Free text, trimmed, at most 64 characters; blank is valid and clears it. Refused with org_matter_code_required when the caller's workspace sets matter_code_policy to required and this is absent or blank.

client_code.description: Free text, trimmed, at most 64 characters; blank is valid. Accepted for backward compatibility: for an org caller the client is always resolved from the matter instead, never from this field.

anyOf.description: Transcription options for this job. Every field is optional; omitting the object requests the account's default behaviour (language auto-detection and speaker labels on).

language_code.description: Force a specific spoken language instead of auto-detection.

speaker_detection.description: Label distinct speakers in the transcript. Forced on automatically when translation_targets is non-empty.

keyterms_prompt.description: Domain vocabulary to bias transcription toward, up to 1000 terms of at most 6 words each.

prompt.description: Free-text context to bias transcription toward.

medical_mode.description: Bill and transcribe as a medical dictation. Requires language_code to be one of en, es, fr, de; billed at a 100 percent surcharge on the duration.

multichannel.description: Transcribe each audio channel independently. Billed per channel: a stereo file counts twice, a 3-channel file three times, up to 8 channels, and the medical surcharge applies on top of that; translation targets stay on a single duration. The channel count is the most channels any audio track of the file carries. A file with more than 8 channels, or one whose channel count cannot be read, falls back to mixed audio with speaker labels and is billed once. Without this option the file is transcribed as one mixed channel and billed once. The initial hold at upload creation is for a single channel; verification raises it to the per-channel amount and fails the job with insufficient_balance if the balance cannot cover it.

translation_targets.description: Locales to additionally translate the transcript into. Each target adds a 25 percent surcharge on the duration and forces speaker_detection on.

auto_generate_insights.description: Override the account's automatic-Insights default for this upload alone. Omit to inherit the account default; an explicit false always suppresses automatic generation for this upload.

get.summary: Fetch a page of presigned direct-to-R2 part URLs
get.description: Returns a fresh page of presigned PUT URLs for the given job's direct-to-R2 upload, starting at the requested part number. Presigned URLs expire, so a client resuming a stalled transfer should call this again rather than reusing URLs from create_upload's response.

parameters.name: job
parameters.description: The upload's job id, returned as job_id by create_upload.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: The first part number to return a URL for.

schema.description: One page of presigned direct-to-R2 PUT URLs, or null when direct-to-R2 uploads are not available for this job and parts must be sent to upload_part instead.

part_size_bytes.description: The byte size of every part except the last.

total_parts.description: The total number of parts this upload is split into.

part_urls.description: Presigned URLs for this page's parts, starting at the requested (or first) part number.

next_part_number.description: The next part number not covered by this page, or null once every part has a URL.

put.summary: Upload one part of a job's audio through this API
put.description: Sends one part's raw bytes to be written into the job's in-progress R2 multipart upload. Only needed when direct-to-R2 presigned URLs are unavailable, or as a fallback for a part whose presigned PUT failed. A repeated PUT of the same part number replaces that part rather than adding to the declared total, so retries are always safe.

parameters.name: job
parameters.description: The upload's job id, returned as job_id by create_upload.

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: The 1-based part number.

post.description: Refreshes the job's activity clock for a direct-to-R2 transfer, whose bytes never pass through this API and so never otherwise refresh it. Call this at an interval well under the 20 minute idle timeout for the whole duration of a long transfer, or the job is reaped mid-flight.

parameters.name: job
parameters.description: The upload's job id, returned as job_id by create_upload.

post.summary: Finish an upload and start transcription
post.description: Marks every declared part as uploaded, probes the assembled object's exact duration, and reconciles the credit hold to the verified billable seconds; if the balance cannot cover the verified total the job is rejected and the hold released rather than run over budget. On success the job moves to queued or processing (reported as queued while verification is still pending) for transcription.

parameters.name: job
parameters.description: The upload's job id, returned as job_id by create_upload.

parts.description: The part number and ETag of every part a direct-to-R2 client uploaded. Omit entirely for a worker-uploaded job.

get.summary: List the account's transcription jobs
get.description: Returns a page of pipeline jobs for the caller's account, newest first. Jobs accumulate for the lifetime of the account, not just while in flight, so this list pages: pass the next_cursor value from one page as the cursor parameter of the next request to page forward; the cursor is opaque and this API refuses one it did not mint rather than silently restarting at page one, since a caller that trusted a silent restart would believe it had paged forward when it had not. Pass active=1 to see only jobs that have not yet reached a terminal state.

parameters.name: active
parameters.description: When set to 1, true or yes, return only jobs that have not reached a terminal state. Any other value, or omitting the parameter, returns every job.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: An opaque paging token from a previous page's next_cursor. Omit to fetch the first page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum rows to return.

get.summary: Read one transcription job
get.description: Returns one pipeline job's current state, billing figures, and transcription options summary. Poll this (or list_jobs) after complete_upload until state reaches done or failed.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The job id.

get.summary: List the account's transcripts
get.description: Returns a page of the caller's transcripts, newest first, with metadata only (no body text). Pass the next_cursor value from one page as the cursor parameter of the next request to page forward; the cursor is opaque and this API refuses one it did not mint rather than silently restarting at page one, since a caller that trusted a silent restart would believe it had paged forward when it had not.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: An opaque paging token from a previous page's next_cursor. Omit to fetch the first page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum rows to return.

get.summary: Read one transcript's metadata and full body
get.description: Returns one transcript's metadata plus its full structured body (the original transcription and any translations, keyed by locale). This is the reference way to fetch a transcript body from this API; format conversion such as SRT, WebVTT or plain text is the caller's job. This route reads the body through the same loader the rest of the backend uses, including its legacy full-envelope path for a transcript stored before the chunked-body protocol existed, so a caller can rely on this route regardless of which storage path actually served a given transcript. The backend's own code calls this whole-body route a rolling-deploy fallback for older clients, alongside the newer manifest and chunk endpoints; that label describes the route itself, not the legacy storage path, and this remains the frozen /v1 way to fetch any transcript's body.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The transcript id.

get.summary: List deletion records for removed transcripts
get.description: Returns a page of the deletion records kept after a transcript is removed, whichever path removed it: an explicit delete, a scheduled deletion, the retention sweep or account deletion. Each record carries the transcript's title, duration and upload time, when and why it was deleted, and the stored deletion receipt. The transcript content itself is gone and cannot be recovered. Records are ordered by the deleted transcript's original upload time, newest first, so they interleave with GET /v1/transcripts by the same key. Pass the next_cursor value from one page as the cursor parameter of the next request to page further back; the cursor is opaque and this API refuses one it did not mint, including a cursor minted by GET /v1/transcripts.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: An opaque paging token from a previous page's next_cursor. Omit to fetch the first page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum rows to return.

get.summary: List purchasable minute packs
get.description: Returns the account's minute-pack catalogue, priced in the account's own currency, including any referral buyer bonus currently available. Read the id of the pack to buy from here before calling buy_minutes. Needs the billing scope AND machine billing switched on for the account in the Hushscript app; either one off is a pat_scope_missing (code 2023) refusal, whichever it was.

post.summary: Charge the account's saved default card for a minute pack
post.description: Charges a saved, fast_checkout_eligible payment method for one pack and credits the account's balance on success. quick_payment_method_id must be the account's current default, except when the account has no default at all, in which case naming an eligible card here makes it the new default. quick_payment_method_id is required: this API can only complete a purchase against a card already on file and has no way to open an interactive Checkout session, so an agent cannot use it to attach a new card. list_saved_cards can only list a card already on file, not create one; add a card first, either through the Hushscript app or by opening the hosted Checkout session create_setup_session returns. A request with no quick_payment_method_id, or a Quick Buy charge that needed authentication, a different payment method, or was declined, is refused outright rather than opened as a Checkout session nobody in this flow could complete. Needs the billing scope AND machine billing switched on for the account in the Hushscript app; either one off is a pat_scope_missing (code 2023) refusal, whichever it was.

pack.description: The id of a pack from list_packs.

idempotency_key.description: A client-minted key preventing a retried request from charging twice.

quick_payment_method_id.description: The id of a card from list_saved_cards, required on this API.

policy_ack.description: Client attestation that the no-refund, instant-delivery notice was shown before this call. Optional; absent is treated as false.

get.summary: List the account's saved payment methods
get.description: Returns every payment method saved on the account plus which one is the current default. This is the only source of a quick_payment_method_id for buy_minutes; it can only list a card already on file, not attach a new one. Needs the billing scope AND machine billing switched on for the account in the Hushscript app; either one off is a pat_scope_missing (code 2023) refusal, whichever it was.

post.summary: Switch which saved card Quick Buy charges
post.description: Sets the given payment method as the account's default, which is the card buy_minutes charges when a caller sends its id as quick_payment_method_id. Use this to switch the default or to pick among multiple eligible cards; buy_minutes only adopts one automatically when the account has no default at all. The id must belong to a payment method already on file, from list_saved_cards; a well formed id this account does not own answers not found, exactly like one that is not a payment method at all. Needs the billing scope AND machine billing switched on for the account in the Hushscript app; either one off is a pat_scope_missing (code 2023) refusal, whichever it was.

payment_method_id.description: The id of a card from list_saved_cards to make the new default.

post.summary: Open a hosted Checkout Session that saves a card with no charge
post.description: Creates a Stripe Checkout Session in setup mode and returns its checkout_url. Open that URL in a browser you control (your own automation, not this API) so Stripe can render the card form and handle any bank authentication itself; card details never pass through this API. No charge is made. Once the caller completes the hosted page, the saved card becomes available from list_saved_cards and can be set as the default with set_default_card; list_saved_cards can lag a just-completed Session by up to 30 seconds, since nothing calls back into this API when the hosted page finishes, so retry rather than concluding the save failed. expires_at is when the Session stops accepting a card; call this endpoint again for a fresh link after that. idempotency_key is optional: omit it and every call opens a new Session, which is safe since a setup Session is never charged and expires on its own; supply your own key only if you want a retried call to land on the same Session instead. Needs the billing scope AND machine billing switched on for the account in the Hushscript app; either one off is a pat_scope_missing (code 2023) refusal, whichever it was.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-minted key so a retried request reuses one Session instead of opening a new one. Omit it for a fresh Session on every call.

get.summary: List the account's purchase history
get.description: Returns a page of the account's past purchases, newest first, each with its settlement status and public receipt reference. Pass the next_cursor value from one page as the cursor parameter of the next request to page further back; the cursor is opaque and this API refuses one it did not mint rather than silently restarting at page one, since a caller that trusted a silent restart would believe it had paged forward when it had not.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: An opaque paging token from a previous page's next_cursor. Omit to fetch the first page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum rows to return.

get.summary: List the account's credit ledger
get.description: Returns a page of the append-only credit ledger, newest first: every hold, settle, release, purchase and refund that has moved the account's second balance, with the job that spent them where there is one. Pass the next_cursor value from one page as the cursor parameter of the next request to page further back; the cursor is opaque and this API refuses one it did not mint rather than silently restarting at page one, since a caller that trusted a silent restart would believe it had paged forward when it had not.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: An opaque paging token from a previous page's next_cursor. Omit to fetch the first page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum rows to return.

get.summary: List the account's active credit holds
get.description: Returns a page of the seconds currently reserved by in-flight work: transcription jobs still running plus unresolved translation, insights and question holds, newest first. Held seconds are not spent yet and are already excluded from the account balance. This is not the ledger: a historical hold entry there may since have been settled or released, while every row here is still outstanding. Pass the next_cursor value from one page as the cursor parameter of the next request to page further back; the cursor is opaque and this API refuses one it did not mint rather than silently restarting at page one.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: An opaque paging token from a previous page's next_cursor. Omit to fetch the first page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum rows to return.

get.summary: Read the caller's organization summary
get.description: A pure passthrough of GET /api/org's body: plan state and term, pool balance and expiry, retention policy, tax id, auto-renewal source and failure count, the workspace-wide default per-member cap, and the caller's own effective cap and month-to-date spend against the pool. Membership only, not admin -- renewal_user_id is visible to admins only.

get.summary: List the caller's organization members
get.description: Returns a page of the caller's organization's members, most recently joined first. Org admin only. Pass the next_cursor value from one page as the cursor parameter of the next request to page further back; the cursor is opaque and this API refuses one it did not mint rather than silently restarting at page one.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: An opaque paging token from a previous page's next_cursor. Omit to fetch the first page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum rows to return.

get.summary: List the caller's organization invoices
get.description: Returns a page of the caller's organization's plan and pack invoices, newest first. Org admin only. Pass the next_cursor value from one page as the cursor parameter of the next request to page further back; the cursor is opaque and this API refuses one it did not mint rather than silently restarting at page one.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: An opaque paging token from a previous page's next_cursor. Omit to fetch the first page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum rows to return.

get.summary: List the caller's organization's firm-custody transcripts
get.description: Returns a page of the caller's organization's firm-custody transcripts, newest first. Reviewer right only (org_reviewer_required if the caller lacks it). Never returns transcript body or title content beyond the title field; opening a transcript body through the transcript read routes is logged to the organization's access log and audit log, and emails the transcript's owner the first time a given reviewer opens it. Pass the next_cursor value from one page as the cursor parameter of the next request to page further back; the cursor is opaque and this API refuses one it did not mint rather than silently restarting at page one.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: An opaque paging token from a previous page's next_cursor. Omit to fetch the first page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum rows to return.

get.summary: List the caller's organization's minute-pool ledger
get.description: Returns a page of the caller's organization's shared minute pool history (holds, settles, releases, purchases), newest first. Org admin only. Pass the next_cursor value from one page as the cursor parameter of the next request to page further back; the cursor is opaque and this API refuses one it did not mint rather than silently restarting at page one.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: An opaque paging token from a previous page's next_cursor. Omit to fetch the first page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum rows to return.

get.summary: List the caller's organization's audit log
get.description: Returns a page of the caller's organization's admin audit log, newest first. Org admin only. Pass the next_cursor value from one page as the cursor parameter of the next request to page further back; the cursor is opaque and this API refuses one it did not mint rather than silently restarting at page one.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: An opaque paging token from a previous page's next_cursor. Omit to fetch the first page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum rows to return.

get.summary: List the caller's organization's matter registry
get.description: Returns up to 200 rows of the caller's organization's matter registry, ordered by code. Membership gated, not admin only: a member filing a transcript under an existing matter is offered this same list. Every row here is {id, code, status} for every caller, including an admin's own token -- the client a matter belongs to is /api admin only: GET /api/org/matters publishes client_id and the client's own code to an admin caller there, but this /v1 route never does, for any caller.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter by registry status. An unrecognized value is refused rather than defaulted.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Case-insensitive prefix match against the matter code.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum rows to return.

400.description: Error response. status was not open or closed.

get.summary: Aggregate the caller's organization's settled spend by member, matter or client
get.description: Aggregates settled minute-pool spend over a bounded range (at most 366 days), grouped by member, by matter code or by client code, and priced at the workspace's own report-only rebill rate. This is the one org read that is not a list: it has no cursor and no paging, since it reports at most one row per member, per matter or per client. Billing gated, like GET /v1/org/ledger, because it aggregates the same org_credit_ledger table.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Range start, Unix seconds, inclusive.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Range end, Unix seconds, exclusive. Must be after from and at most 366 days later.

parameters.name: group_by
parameters.description: How to group the aggregated rows. An unrecognized value is refused rather than defaulted.

422.description: Error response. from/to formed an invalid or oversized range, or group_by was not member, matter or client.

get.summary: Download the caller's organization's settled spend by member, matter or client as CSV
get.description: Same aggregation as GET /v1/org/usage, downloaded as a CSV file instead of a JSON body.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Range start, Unix seconds, inclusive.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Range end, Unix seconds, exclusive. Must be after from and at most 366 days later.

parameters.name: group_by
parameters.description: How to group the aggregated rows. An unrecognized value is refused rather than defaulted.

200.description: Success. A CSV file, one row per group.

422.description: Error response. from/to formed an invalid or oversized range, or group_by was not member, matter or client.

get.summary: Download the caller's organization's whole minute-pool ledger as CSV
get.description: Downloads the caller's organization's entire org_credit_ledger history (not paged, unlike GET /v1/org/ledger) as a CSV file. Sets X-Hushscript-Csv-Truncated: 1 if the export hit its internal page ceiling.

200.description: Success. A CSV file, one row per ledger entry, newest first.

get.summary: Download the caller's organization's whole audit log as CSV
get.description: Downloads the caller's organization's entire org_audit_log history (not paged, unlike GET /v1/org/audit) as a CSV file, with the same detail redaction GET /v1/org/audit applies. Sets X-Hushscript-Csv-Truncated: 1 if the export hit its internal page ceiling.

200.description: Success. A CSV file, one row per audit entry, newest first.

post.summary: Schedule the private to firm custody switch
post.description: Org admin only. Schedules the workspace's custody mode to switch from private to firm a fixed notice period from now, and mails every member. Nothing changes immediately: a daily background lane flips the mode once the notice period expires. Only the value firm is accepted; a switch from firm back to private is not supported here, since transcripts already stamped under firm custody would silently change custodian.

custody.description: Must be firm; this route only schedules the private to firm switch.

switch_at.description: Unix timestamp when the switch to firm custody takes effect.

409.description: Error response. The workspace is already firm, a switch is already scheduled, or the request asked for anything other than firm.

patch.summary: Change a workspace member's rights or cap
patch.description: Admin only. Sets any subset of the member's is_admin, is_billing and is_reviewer rights, and their per-member monthly cap in seconds. At least one field must be present. Demoting the workspace's last remaining admin is refused, evaluated inside the same atomic update so two concurrent demotions cannot both succeed and strand the workspace with no admin.

parameters.name: user_id
parameters.description: The member's user id.

is_admin.description: Grant or revoke the admin right. Omit to leave unchanged.

is_billing.description: Grant or revoke the billing right. Omit to leave unchanged.

is_reviewer.description: Grant or revoke the reviewer right. Omit to leave unchanged.

monthly_cap_seconds.description: The member's monthly spend cap in seconds against the pool, or null to clear it. Omit to leave unchanged.

404.description: Error response. The target user is not a member of this workspace.

409.description: Error response. The change would leave the workspace with no remaining admin.

422.description: Error response. No field was present, or monthly_cap_seconds fell outside the allowed range.

post.summary: Place a legal hold on a transcript
post.description: Reviewer only. Places a legal hold on one transcript in the caller's firm-custody workspace. A held transcript is exempt from the retention sweep, the retention re-clamp sweep and ordinary deletion, and its body, translations, cleaned text and AI outputs cannot be edited or regenerated (409 transcript_legal_hold), until the hold is lifted.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The transcript id.

404.description: Error response. No such transcript in this workspace.

delete.summary: Lift a legal hold on a transcript
delete.description: Reviewer only. Lifts a legal hold on one transcript in the caller's firm-custody workspace. A held transcript is exempt from the retention sweep, the retention re-clamp sweep and ordinary deletion, and its body, translations, cleaned text and AI outputs cannot be edited or regenerated (409 transcript_legal_hold), until the hold is lifted.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The transcript id.

404.description: Error response. No such transcript in this workspace.

get.summary: Read the account's saved transcription context
get.description: Returns every saved dictionary and prompt preset on the account. A dictionary teaches the transcriber names and terms it would otherwise mishear; a prompt preset is standing free-text guidance. Both can be selected by id on an upload. This response is not paginated and carries no cursor: an account may hold at most 50 dictionaries and 20 prompt presets, both enforced when they are created, so a single response is always the complete set.

post.summary: Start a headless, payment-first account signup
post.description: Opens a hosted Stripe Checkout Session for a payment-first, headless account signup. No account and no session cookie exist yet: complete checkout_url with your own browser automation, then claim the account with claim_secret at POST /v1/agent/accounts/{signup_id}/claim. Every field is validated before any Stripe call, followed by the same restricted-jurisdiction and allowlist gates the human signup paths apply. accept_terms_version must equal the server's current policy version, returned in the policy_version_stale error when it does not match. pack selects a minute pack by id; amount and currency come back server derived and must never be sent in the request. data_region is derived from your network location and an optional hint is honored only when it agrees with that derivation. signup_id is region-prefixed (hsr1:<region>:<id>) and must be presented back verbatim to the claim route, so the request reaches the same regional backend that holds the row. Set dry_run to true to validate the request and get back a synthetic 200 response with no Stripe session created and no charge possible, for rehearsing the shape before spending real money; a dry run signup_id is never region-prefixed and can never be claimed.

200.description: Success (dry_run only). Same shape as 201, but no Stripe session was created and no agent_signups row was written; signup_id is prefixed dry_ and can never be claimed.

post.summary: Claim a paid agent signup into a real account
post.description: Exchanges a paid, unclaimed agent signup for the account it pays for. Presents the claim_secret returned once by POST /v1/agent/accounts; a wrong secret, an unknown signup_id, an already claimed signup, a refunded signup, and an expired signup all answer the identical agent_claim_invalid error so a caller can never learn which of those is true. Only once that secret checks out does payment state matter: a signup whose Checkout Session has not settled to paid answers wrong_state instead. A successful claim is single use; creates exactly one account with a synthetic, unresolvable login identity; grants the paid pack once, never twice, even on a retried request; and mints exactly one personal access token with the account's own agent scopes, returned only in this response.

Atomically mints a successor personal access token and revokes the one that authenticated this request. A machine account has no password and no usable mailbox, so this is its only way to rotate a leaked credential. The successor keeps the predecessor's scopes, billing_enabled flag, name, client_label, and expiry policy; only the secret changes. The predecessor fails authentication on the very next request. This route references no token but the one that called it: it cannot list, mint, or revoke any other credential.

BearerAuth.description: Either a Hushscript session bearer token or a Personal Access Token. A Personal Access Token is further restricted to the scope named in the operation's x-required-scope extension; a request whose token lacks that scope is refused with pat_scope_missing (code 2023), and a route with no scope mapping at all is refused with pat_forbidden (code 2022) before the token's scopes are even read. The billing scope carries a second, account-wide condition: it stays inert unless the account owner has also switched machine billing on for the account in the Hushscript app, which no token of any scope can do for them. A token that holds the billing scope while that account switch is off is refused with the same pat_scope_missing (code 2023), so a 2023 from a billing operation does not on its own mean the token is missing the scope, and re-minting the token with the scope again will not clear it.

InternalError.description: Internal error. The delegated /api result could not be projected into a /v1 body, or an unrelated internal fault was logged; every /v1 operation can reach this. See internal_error in x-error-catalog.

RateLimited.description: Too many requests. Every /v1 operation authenticates through the same chokepoint that enforces a per-token request budget for a PAT caller (PAT_LIMITER, 1200 requests/60s); POST /v1/billing/setup-session, POST /v1/billing/purchase, POST /v1/billing/cards/default and GET /v1/billing/cards (when it has to read the cards from Stripe) additionally enforce a tighter per-account budget (PAT_BILLING_LIMITER, 60 requests/60s) before making any Stripe call, and POST /v1/uploads separately enforces its own burst limiter (UPLOAD_LIMITER), keyed per user and also per IP (a looser budget) for a PAT caller, and per IP for a session caller. A PAT-throttled refusal carries a Retry-After header; the uploads burst limiter does not. POST /v1/billing/purchase can also answer 429 for a distinct reason, for an agent account and for a human account's PAT caller: the purchase cap per rolling window (see agent_purchase_capped in x-error-catalog), carrying details.limit, details.window_seconds and details.retry_after_seconds alongside its own Retry-After header. See rate_limited in x-error-catalog for the ordinary case.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying. Present on a PAT_LIMITER or PAT_BILLING_LIMITER refusal, and on an agent_purchase_capped refusal; absent on the /v1/uploads burst limiter.

Error.description: The frozen /v1 error body. error and code are always present together; the remaining keys are optional detail this API includes only when the specific error carries them, and they are omitted rather than emitted as null when absent.

error.description: The error's slug. See x-error-catalog for the full list.

code.description: The error's stable numeric code. See x-error-catalog. Never reused or renumbered.

needed_seconds.description: Seconds the failed action needed. Present on a balance-shortfall error.

balance_seconds.description: The account's personal balance in seconds. Present on a personal balance-shortfall error.

held_seconds.description: Seconds already committed to other in-flight jobs. Present alongside balance_seconds.

org_balance_seconds.description: The organization's shared pool balance in seconds. Present on an org-funded balance-shortfall error instead of balance_seconds.

details.description: Structured recovery detail for an error that is not a plain balance shortfall. Present on agent_pack_locked and agent_purchase_capped.

allowed_packs.description: Pack ids the agent account may buy right now. Present on agent_pack_locked; retry with one of these.

limit.description: The per-credential purchase cap for the rolling window. Present on agent_purchase_capped.

window_seconds.description: The length of the rolling window in seconds. Present on agent_purchase_capped.

retry_after_seconds.description: Seconds until the oldest purchase counted toward the cap leaves the window. Present on agent_purchase_capped; matches the Retry-After header.

UploadLimits.description: The caller's current upload admission limits, shared by every response that carries them.

max_daily_seconds.description: The account's daily transcription-minutes cap, in seconds.

max_active_jobs.description: The maximum number of concurrent pipeline jobs this account may have in flight.

active_jobs.description: How many pipeline jobs are currently in flight.

used_today_seconds.description: Billable seconds already used today, in the account's own rolling day.

balance_seconds.description: Net balance in seconds: the raw balance minus any clawback debt. May be negative.

held_seconds.description: Seconds currently committed to in-flight jobs and not yet settled.

credits_expire_at.description: Unix seconds after which the balance expires without a completed transcription or purchase, or null if no expiry is currently armed.

data_region.description: The region this account's data lives in, e.g. us, eu, apac or oc.

n.description: The 1-based part number this URL is for.

url.description: A presigned R2 PUT URL, valid for a limited time.

balance_seconds.description: The account's net balance after this upload's hold was placed.

upload.description: One page of presigned direct-to-R2 PUT URLs, or null when direct-to-R2 uploads are not available for this job and parts must be sent to upload_part instead.

part_size_bytes.description: The byte size of every part except the last.

total_parts.description: The total number of parts this upload is split into.

part_urls.description: Presigned URLs for this page's parts, starting at the requested (or first) part number.

next_part_number.description: The next part number not covered by this page, or null once every part has a URL.

funding.description: Which balance this upload's hold was placed against.

state.description: The job's initial state, typically uploading.
The job's state immediately after completion, e.g. queued, processing or done.

verified_seconds.description: The probed exact duration, once verification has run; null while verification is still pending.

balance_seconds.description: The account's net balance after the hold was reconciled to the verified duration.

OptionsSummary.description: A content-free summary of the transcription options a job was submitted with: what was requested, never the free-text content itself.

language_code.description: The manually forced language, or null if language auto-detection was used.

keyterms.description: Whether a keyterms prompt was set. The terms themselves are not included.

prompt.description: Whether a free-text context prompt was set. The prompt itself is not included.

auto_generate_insights.description: This upload's override of automatic Insights generation, or null if it used the account default.

state.description: One of uploading, fetching, queued, processing, done or failed.

verified_seconds.description: The probed exact duration, once known.

error.description: A short failure reason when state is failed, otherwise null.

failure_kind.description: Set when the file itself could not be read: `media_unreadable` when the upload could not be probed as audio, `media_undecodable` when the transcription provider could not decode it. Either way the file needs converting (for example to MP3 or WAV) and uploading again; nothing was charged and the hold was released. Null for every other job, including failures of any other kind and jobs that failed before this field existed.

retry_of.description: The id of an earlier failed job of yours that this job retries, set when the browser app re-uploaded a converted copy of an unreadable file, otherwise null.

transcript_id.description: The resulting transcript's id, once transcription has finished.

fetched_bytes.description: Bytes fetched so far for a from-url import. Present only while a fetch is in progress.

fetch_total_bytes.description: The total byte size a from-url import is fetching toward. Present only while a fetch is in progress.

next_cursor.description: An opaque token for the next page's cursor parameter, or null on the last page. This API refuses a cursor it did not mint.

translations.description: Keyed by target locale, plus the reserved key cleaned for the AI-rewritten cleaned body when one exists.

speaker_names.description: Provider speaker label mapped to a display name, for every speaker the caller has renamed.

auto_delete_at.description: When this transcript is scheduled to be purged, or null to keep it indefinitely.

edited.description: Whether the original body has been edited since transcription.

matter_code.description: The workspace matter this transcript is filed under, or null. Set at upload time and editable afterwards; always null for a transcript that was never funded by a workspace.

client_code.description: The workspace client this transcript is filed under, or null. Set at upload time and editable afterwards; always null for a transcript that was never funded by a workspace.

insights_state.description: A display hint only, never an authority on whether Insights may be generated or charged for.

next_cursor.description: An opaque token for the next page's cursor parameter, or null on the last page. This API refuses a cursor it did not mint.

amount.description: The price in minor units of currency, already localized for the account's country.

referral_bonus_seconds.description: Extra seconds this purchase would add from an available referral buyer bonus. Zero when none is available.

available.description: Whether the caller's account may buy this pack right now. Present for agent accounts only: an agent's pack tier gates the larger packs until enough prior payments have settled past the dispute window. Absent on every human caller's response, whose packs are all always available.

balance_seconds.description: The account's net balance after this purchase settled.

id.description: Use this value as quick_payment_method_id when it is is_default and fast_checkout_eligible. If default_id is null, naming any fast_checkout_eligible card here also makes it the new default.

fast_checkout_eligible.description: Whether this method may be charged off-session by buy_minutes.

checkout_url.description: Open this URL in a browser you control to complete the hosted setup page.

expires_at.description: Unix timestamp after which the Session stops accepting a card.

receipt_number.description: The public receipt reference, e.g. HS-20260101-abcdef0123456789-1.

next_cursor.description: An opaque token for the next page's cursor parameter, or null on the last page. This API refuses a cursor it did not mint.
An opaque token for the next page's cursor parameter, or null on the last page. This API refuses a cursor it did not mint.

kind.description: Which kind of work reserved these seconds. The id is that work's own id and is unique only within its kind.

next_cursor.description: An opaque token for the next page's cursor parameter, or null on the last page. This API refuses a cursor it did not mint.

created_at.description: When the transcript was originally uploaded, Unix seconds. This is the key the list is ordered and paged on.

cause.description: Which deletion path removed the transcript: an explicit delete (manual), the transcript's own auto_delete_at retention date (scheduled), the dormant-account purge (dormant), or the global retention sweep (expired).

receipt.description: The receipt recorded when the transcript was deleted, kept so the deletion stays evidenced after the content itself is gone. Null when the stored receipt could not be read back.

next_cursor.description: An opaque token for the next page's cursor parameter, or null on the last page. This API refuses a cursor it did not mint.

canonical.description: The spelling the transcript should use.

variants.description: Alternative spellings that should be normalized to the canonical form.

category.description: What kind of term this is. Never empty and never null: an entry saved without a category is stored as other.

note.description: Free-text note about the entry. Empty when unset; never null.

description.description: Free-text description. Empty when unset; never null.

language_code.description: The language this applies to: all, or one of the supported source language codes. Never empty and never null: unset is stored as all.

terms.description: The flat recognition terms this dictionary compiles into. Derived from entries when entries exist (every canonical spelling and its variants, deduplicated); otherwise the legacy flat list stored before entries existed.

is_default.description: Whether this dictionary is applied to an upload that selects none explicitly. At most one dictionary is the default.

description.description: Free-text description. Empty when unset; never null.

language_code.description: The language this applies to: all, or one of the supported source language codes. Never empty and never null: unset is stored as all.

TranscriptionContextResponse.description: Not paginated and carrying no cursor: both collections are capped when they are written (50 dictionaries, 20 prompt presets), so this response is always complete.

monthly_cap_seconds.description: This member's own monthly seconds cap, or null when unset.

next_cursor.description: An opaque token for the next page's cursor parameter, or null on the last page. This API refuses a cursor it did not mint.
An opaque token for the next page's cursor parameter, or null on the last page. This API refuses a cursor it did not mint.

OrgTranscript.description: One row of the organization's firm-custody transcript index. Never carries transcript body or content beyond the title.

next_cursor.description: An opaque token for the next page's cursor parameter, or null on the last page. This API refuses a cursor it did not mint.
An opaque token for the next page's cursor parameter, or null on the last page. This API refuses a cursor it did not mint.
An opaque token for the next page's cursor parameter, or null on the last page. This API refuses a cursor it did not mint.

key.description: The member email, matter code or client code this row aggregates, or "(none)" for an unfiled job or a purged member.

cost_cents.description: billed_seconds priced at the workspace's rebill_rate_cents_per_hour, rounded up to the cent.

AgentSignupRequest.description: The client must never supply amount: it is derived server side from pack.

contact_email.description: Address for receipts and notices only. Never used to sign in; the created account has no login path of its own.

pack_id.description: Which minute pack to buy. See GET /v1/billing/packs for the catalogue.

accept_terms_version.description: Must equal the server's current policy version or the request is refused with policy_version_stale, which names the current value.

data_region.description: Optional region hint. Honored only when it agrees with the region derived from your network location; otherwise the derived region is used silently.

dry_run.description: Validate the request and return a synthetic response with no Stripe session and no charge. Defaults to false.

signup_id.description: Region-prefixed (hsr1:<region>:<id>), e.g. hsr1:eu:4c3a1f9e7b2d4e6f8a0c1b2d3e4f5061. Present it back verbatim as the path segment when claiming the account. A dry_run response's signup_id is prefixed dry_ instead and can never be claimed.

claim_secret.description: Returned exactly once. Only its hash is stored; there is no way to recover it later.

checkout_url.description: Open this URL in a browser you control to complete the hosted Checkout page.

amount.description: Charge amount in the currency's minor unit.

expires_at.description: Unix timestamp after which the Session stops accepting a card.

claim_secret.description: The secret returned exactly once by POST /v1/agent/accounts.

user_id.description: The account created by this claim. There is no login path for it; authenticate with pat instead.

pat.description: Returned exactly once. Only its hash is stored; there is no way to recover it later.

balance_seconds.description: The account's balance immediately after the pack this signup paid for was granted.

pat.description: The successor token, returned exactly once. Only its hash is stored; there is no way to recover it later. The predecessor that authenticated this request stops working immediately.

scopes.description: The scopes carried by pat, identical to the predecessor's.

expires_at.description: The successor's expiry policy, carried over from the predecessor unchanged. Null when the predecessor never expired.

role.description: The caller's own role in this organization: admin or member.

plan_term.description: annual or monthly, or null if the org has never had a plan.

plan_active_until.description: Unix seconds the current term runs until, or null before the org's first plan is paid.

plan_active.description: Whether the term itself is still running (ignores grace).

seats_pending.description: Seats held by pending, unexpired invites.

balance_seconds.description: The pool's raw balance. Can be negative after a void clawback or a negative pool adjustment.

spendable_seconds.description: balance_seconds floored at zero, and zeroed outright when the org is outside its funding window (frozen or lapsed past grace).

pool_expires_at.description: Unix seconds the pool's own rolling 365-day expiry falls at, re-anchored on every credit and every settle. Null if the pool has never held a positive balance.

billing_email.description: The workspace's billing contact. Null unless the caller is an admin or holds the billing right.

billing_details.description: Free-text billing details shown on invoices. Null when none are set, and always null unless the caller is an admin or holds the billing right.

tax_id.description: The buyer's self-declared tax id, shown on invoices. Not validated against any registry. Null unless the caller is an admin or holds the billing right.

tax_id_label.description: The buyer's own word for tax_id, e.g. VAT, EIN, ABN. Null unless the caller is an admin or holds the billing right.

renewal_capped.description: Whether renewal_failures has reached the cap the daily renewal lane stops retrying at.

renewal_source_stored.description: Whether a saved card is on file for the renewal lane to charge. Never the payment method id itself.

renewal_user_id.description: The id of the member whose saved card the renewal lane charges. Visible to admins only; a non-admin member always sees null here regardless of whether a source is stored (see renewal_source_stored).

member_cap_seconds.description: The workspace-wide default per-member monthly spending cap against the pool. Null means no org-wide default.

caller_effective_cap_seconds.description: The signed-in caller's own effective monthly cap: their personal override if one is set, else member_cap_seconds, else null for no cap. Also null when the caller is outside the org's current funding window.

caller_spent_seconds_this_month.description: The signed-in caller's own month-to-date spend against the pool. Null under the same condition caller_effective_cap_seconds is null.

is_owner.description: Whether the signed-in caller is the workspace's single transferable owner (distinct from is_admin).

owner_user_id.description: The id of the workspace's transferable owner, visible to every member. Falls back to the org's creator if owner_user_id was never explicitly set on the row.

custody.description: private or firm. private: transcripts belong to the member, no reviewer can open them. firm: a transcript created while a member belongs to the workspace is workspace property; is_reviewer members can open it.

custody_switch_at.description: Unix seconds the pending private-to-firm switch takes effect, or null when no switch is scheduled. Only ever set while custody is still private.

retention_reclamp_at.description: Unix seconds the currently armed retention re-clamp takes effect, or null when none is scheduled. Set only while a tightened max_retention_days still has existing transcripts left to pull in.

retention_reclamp_days.description: The retention day count the armed re-clamp will apply, or null when none is scheduled. Mirrors max_retention_days at the moment the re-clamp was armed, not necessarily the current value.

x-error-catalog.meaning: The request body could not be parsed, or a required field was missing. Check the request against this operation's schema and resend.
The email address failed format or safety validation (address lists, spoofed display names, control characters and quoted local parts are all rejected). Send a single plain address.
The password did not meet the length bounds this API enforces. Choose a password between the documented minimum and maximum byte length.

No longer emitted: GET /api/auth/verify without a token now redirects to the app with ?error=link_expired instead of returning this JSON error. It stays in the catalog, with its code, slug and status unchanged, for clients that may still key on it.
The requested locale is not one this account or API supports. Use one of the documented locale codes.
The part number is outside the plan for this upload (below 1 or past the last part for the declared size). Recompute the part count from the declared size and part size.
No payment method was available to complete this action. Add or select a saved payment method before retrying.
An inbound webhook or event payload could not be parsed or verified. This is not actionable from a normal API client.

No longer emitted: no current route returns this code. It stays in the catalog, with its code, slug and status unchanged, for clients that may still key on it. It used to mean: The uploaded file's name failed validation. Rename the file to remove unsupported characters and retry.
The declared or verified duration is shorter than 15 seconds or longer than this API's maximum accepted length of 10 hours. Trim or split the recording before uploading.
The declared byte size is zero or exceeds this API's maximum accepted upload size. Compress or split the file before uploading.
One uploaded part exceeded the maximum part size this API accepts. Resend that part split into smaller chunks.
The bytes received for this upload would exceed the size declared at creation. Start a new upload with the correct declared size.
The upload was marked complete with no parts recorded. Upload at least one part before calling complete.
The provided title exceeded the maximum length or contained disallowed content. Shorten or sanitize the title and retry.
The speaker-name mapping was not valid JSON or exceeded the allowed shape. Send a flat object of speaker label to display name.
The speaker-name mapping named more speakers than this API allows on one transcript. Remove entries before retrying.
The preview clip could not be read as audio. Send a supported audio format within the preview size and duration limits.
The preview clip exceeds the maximum preview duration. Trim the clip and retry.

No longer emitted: no current route returns this code. It stays in the catalog, with its code, slug and status unchanged, for clients that may still key on it. It used to mean: The audio container or codec could not be probed by this API. Re-encode to one of the documented supported formats.
The requested pack id does not exist in this account's catalogue. Read GET /v1/billing/packs for the current, valid pack ids.
The transcription_options object failed validation (an unsupported language, an invalid combination of options, or an over-limit field). Re-check each option against its documented bounds.
The submitted transcript edit was not valid for the current body (bad utterance shape or an out-of-range index). Reload the current body before editing.
The request would leave more tags on the transcript than this API allows. Remove existing tags before adding new ones.
No speech was detected in the submitted audio. Confirm the source file actually contains an audio track with speech.
The supplied source URL is not a well-formed https URL. Provide a direct https link to the audio or video file.
The supplied URL resolves to a host or address this API refuses to fetch (internal ranges, this API's own storage, or a disallowed host). Use a public, third-party hosted URL instead.
This URL source needs interactive authentication this API cannot perform on the caller's behalf. Download the file yourself and upload the bytes directly instead.
The supplied idempotency_key was outside the accepted length bounds. Send a key between the documented minimum and maximum length, or omit it.
The assembled object was shorter than the size declared at creation, so the hold was released and nothing was billed. Re-upload every part and call complete again.

This API is already fetching from that target host as fast as it will, so the fetch was refused before it was attempted. This bounds the target site, not the caller: a different source URL will go through immediately, and the same one will after a short wait.
accept_terms_version did not match the server's current policy version. The server records its own value, never the caller's, so retry with the current version returned by this same error.

The bearer token is missing, malformed, expired, or revoked. This is also the answer for a revoked, malformed, or unknown Personal Access Token, so a caller holding a PAT should mint a fresh one rather than retry the same one. Obtain a fresh session token or Personal Access Token and retry with it in the Authorization header.
The submitted email/password pair did not match an account. Check the credentials or use the password-reset flow.
The Cloudflare Turnstile challenge could not be verified. Re-run the challenge on the client and resend with a fresh token.
This action is not available from the caller's detected jurisdiction. This is a policy decision, not a transient failure; retrying will not help.
New account creation is currently closed for this signup path. Retry later or use an already-provisioned account.
The account is suspended, most commonly due to an open payment dispute. Resolve the dispute or contact support before retrying.
A cryptographic signature on this request could not be verified. Not reachable from this public API; indicates a caller configuration bug elsewhere in the stack.

This action requires the caller to belong to an organization, and the bearer does not. Join or create an organization first. PATCH /api/org also answers it, writing nothing, when the patch names a field whose right the caller lacks: the billing contact, tax identity and auto_renew need the billing right, every other field the admin right. POST /api/org/invites and PATCH /api/org/members/:user_id answer it too when they hand out or take away the billing right (an invite carrying an explicit is_billing true; a patch naming is_billing) for a caller who does not hold it, except that while no member of the workspace holds the right any admin may grant it (a revoke always needs it). A workspace member removal answers it too when the target holds the billing right and the caller neither holds it nor is that member (a member may always leave; removing a holder needs the right, so the recovery rule above is reachable only after the last holder leaves, revokes their own right, or deletes their account). An invite that leaves is_billing out defaults it to the caller's own right for role admin, so an admin without the billing right inviting an admin sends a plain admin invite and is not refused.
This route is not in the Personal Access Token scope map at all, so no token, regardless of scope, can reach it. Use a session bearer for this call instead.
The Personal Access Token does not carry the scope this route requires (see x-required-scope on the operation). Mint or use a token that includes it.

Deleting an account needs proof it is the holder asking. DELETE /api/me carried neither current_password nor email_code, or sent current_password for a password set or changed in the last 7 days, or one the requesting session itself set. Send the current password (set more than 7 days ago, not by this session), or a code sent by POST /api/me/deletion-code.

No longer emitted: no current route returns this code. It stays in the catalog, with its code, slug and status unchanged, for clients that may still key on it. It used to mean: This purchase needs a card on file and the account has none. Add a card through the account's payment settings before retrying.
The account's balance cannot cover the requested seconds. The error body's needed_seconds and balance_seconds report the shortfall; top up before retrying.

No longer emitted: no current route returns this code. It stays in the catalog, with its code, slug and status unchanged, for clients that may still key on it. It used to mean: The card on file was declined when charged. Use a different payment method or contact the card issuer.
The organization's shared minute pool cannot cover the requested seconds. The error body's org_balance_seconds reports the pool's current balance; an org admin must top it up.
No resource exists at this id for the authenticated caller. Confirm the id and that it belongs to this account.
The target resource is not in a state this action allows (for example, an upload that already finished). Read its current state before retrying.
An account already exists for this email address. Sign in instead of registering again.
This action cannot proceed while the account has active transcription jobs. Wait for them to finish, or cancel them, then retry.

No longer emitted: no current route returns this code. It stays in the catalog, with its code, slug and status unchanged, for clients that may still key on it. It used to mean: An Insights bundle already exists for this transcript and this call did not ask for a paid regeneration. Pass a mode to request one.
This promo code has already been redeemed on this account. Each code may be redeemed once per account.

Creating an organization: the caller founded another organization that is still unpaid and either is still a member of it or created it less than 7 days ago (one unpaid founded organization at a time; leaving it does not lift the bound inside the 7 days and does after them; belonging to other organizations does not block it). Accepting an invite: the account is already a member of that organization.
The organization has no active plan, so its pool cannot fund this action. An org admin must renew the plan.
The organization is already at its seat limit. Remove a member or increase the plan's seat count before inviting another.
The target account's data region does not match the organization's region. Cross-region membership is not supported; the user needs an account in the org's region.
The magic link or similar time-boxed link has expired. Request a new one.
The referenced token or session has expired. Request a fresh one and retry.
The submitted one-time code does not match what was issued. Re-check the code or request a new one.

No longer emitted: no current route returns this code. It stays in the catalog, with its code, slug and status unchanged, for clients that may still key on it. It used to mean: There is no pending operation of this kind to act on (for example, no pending export). Start the operation before trying to read its result.
This promo code is not currently redeemable (expired, not yet active, or exhausted). Check the promotion's terms.
This promo requires a verified card on file before it can be redeemed. Add a card first.
No invoice exists at this id for the caller's organization. Confirm the invoice id from GET /api/org/invoices.
The requested retention setting exceeds the organization's configured maximum. Request a value at or below the org's ceiling.
The organization already has an open, unpaid plan invoice. Settle or wait for it to be superseded before requesting another.
The OAuth handoff exchange code is invalid, already used, or expired. Restart the handoff flow to obtain a new code.

The POST /api/pats request body failed validation: an empty or oversized name, an unknown or empty scope list, created_via outside app or oauth, or an invalid client_label. Fix the request body and retry. A bearer token that is itself malformed, revoked, or unknown never reaches this code; that case answers unauthorized (2000) instead.

This purchase needs full Checkout, which this API cannot open or let the caller complete. Either the request had no quick_payment_method_id, in which case resend with one set to a card already on file (see GET /v1/billing/cards), or the saved card will not go through as attempted (declined, needs a different payment method, or was canceled), in which case retrying the same card changes nothing: fix or replace it, then retry with a brand new idempotency_key, or complete the purchase from the Hushscript app. A card whose issuer wants an interactive challenge is not a decline and answers 4023 instead.
The account already holds the maximum number of Personal Access Tokens. Revoke an unused token before minting another.

The saved card is fine, but the issuer wants a challenge (3DS) before this charge can go through. This API cannot open or let the caller complete that challenge, so the purchase is refused rather than left pending. Complete the purchase from the Hushscript app instead, where the holder can go through authentication.

Creating a new organization is closed in this environment. Signups are open in every environment today, so this answers only where they were deliberately closed again. Existing organizations keep working normally; every other org route, including renewals, pack purchases, invites, and admin reads, stays open.

The organization's plan lapsed and its 30 day grace window has also passed, so no new organization funded upload is admitted. A job already running still settles normally. Paying a plan renewal clears the freeze right away.

The organization's shared minute pool is present but its 365-day rolling clock has lapsed with no purchase, grant, or completed job to renew it. A pack purchase, an included plan grant, or completing another org-funded job all restart the clock for another year.

This pool member has used their whole monthly share of the workspace's pooled seconds. The workspace pool itself may still have a balance; this is the per-member cap, separate from a plain insufficient-balance refusal.

The daily renewal lane charged the organization's stored renewal card and Stripe answered with a structured failure. The invoice stays issued, the failure count goes up by one, a renewal-failed email carrying a fresh Checkout link for that same invoice is sent (flagged as the final attempt once the count reaches the cap of 3), and the lapsed term falls into the ordinary grace window. Once the cap is reached the lane stops retrying this organization automatically -- no further charge attempts, no further emails -- until the open invoice is paid by hand, which resets the count. GET /api/org exposes this as a derived renewal_capped boolean.

The chosen payment method is not one of the caller's own saved, fast checkout eligible cards, the caller has no Stripe customer at all, or auto renew was switched on with no renewal card stored yet. All three answer identically so this route can never be used to learn whether a given payment method id exists.

The operator's signed fee-refund command came more than 30 days after the workspace's plan was first paid for, so the plan fee refund window has closed. No customer route returns this code; the fee refund exists only as that operator command. Packs are never refundable and never reach this check.

The target invoice of the operator's signed fee-refund command is not a paid, unrefunded plan invoice of this workspace, or the workspace already took its one refund. No customer route returns this code; the fee refund exists only as that operator command. Packs are never refundable regardless of this check.

No longer emitted: no current route returns this code. It stays in the catalog, with its code, slug and status unchanged, for clients that may still key on it. The signed admin fee-refund command answers its own currency_mismatch refusal instead. It used to mean: The Stripe charge settled in a currency different from the invoice's currency, so a partial refund amount cannot be computed. Contact support for a manual refund.
The tax id or its label does not match a shape this system accepts. This is a shape check only, never a registry lookup against a tax authority.
A signup already exists for this contact_email and has not yet been claimed, refunded, or expired. Wait for it to resolve or use a different contact address.

The claim secret did not match, or the signup does not exist, has already been claimed, was refunded, or has expired. These cases answer identically on purpose. A confirmed-but-unpaid Checkout Session answers wrong_state (4001) instead once the secret itself has checked out.

An agent account's pack tier does not allow the requested pack yet. A fresh agent account is limited to the small packs; a larger pack unlocks only once enough prior payments have settled past the dispute window. Reached on POST /v1/agent/accounts (signup, always tier 0) and POST /v1/billing/purchase for an agent caller. The response carries details.allowed_packs, the pack ids currently buyable; retry with one of those. Never reached by a human account.

An agent account has reached its per-credential spend cap for the current rolling window: 3 purchases, paid or declined, in the trailing 24 hours. The cap is counted per account across every credential the account has ever held, not per token, so rotating a credential does not reset it. Reached on POST /v1/billing/purchase for an agent caller, and for a human account's personal access token caller, which has its own cap of the same size counted the same way. A human purchasing through the app is never capped. The response carries details.limit, details.window_seconds and details.retry_after_seconds, and a Retry-After header naming the same wait in seconds.

A rights change or a member removal would leave the workspace with no member carrying is_admin. This is refused by a count check evaluated inside the update itself, not by a pre-read, so two admins concurrently dropping each other's flag cannot both succeed.
The member rights update carried no changed field, or monthly_cap_seconds fell outside the allowed range for a pooled member cap.

The requested custody change is refused: the workspace is already firm custody, a custody switch is already scheduled, or the request asks to move to private custody, which is not reversible once transcripts carry an org_id.
The route needs the reviewer right. Carrying the admin flag alone never satisfies it, since the reviewer right is kept deliberately separate.
Offboarding a member from a firm-custody workspace named no custodian to receive that member's work product.
The named custodian is not a reviewer member of this workspace, or is the member being removed. The admin right does not qualify on its own.

Deletion, an edit (body, translation, cleaned text, revert, retranslate), an AI-output delete or paid regeneration, a retention change or a re-file to another matter was refused because the transcript is under a legal hold, placed by a workspace admin or derived from its matter.
The request named a workspace that the caller does not belong to.
The workspace sets matter_code_policy to required and the upload carried no matter_code. Send one, or ask a workspace admin to relax the policy.

matter_code or client_code is longer than 64 characters after trimming. Both are free text fields checked on length alone, and a blank or whitespace-only value is accepted and stored as no code. For a workspace (org) upload, client_code is validated here but the stored value always comes from the resolved matter's client, never from this field; a personal (no org) upload's client_code is stored exactly as sent.
GET /api/org/usage: from or to is missing, not a positive unix timestamp, reversed, or spans more than 366 days.
GET /api/org/usage: group_by is present and is not member, matter or client.
PATCH /api/org: rebill_rate_cents_per_hour is negative or above 100000. The rate is report only and never charges anyone.
A workspace dictionary or prompt preset was created, edited or deleted by a member who holds neither the admin nor the reviewer right.
The workspace already owns the maximum number of dictionaries or prompt presets. Delete one first before creating another.
PATCH /api/org: letterhead failed shape or length validation. Send null to clear the letterhead instead.
POST or DELETE /api/org/holds/matter from a workspace that is not in firm custody, or from a member without the reviewer right.
POST /api/org/holds/matter: no workspace transcript carries that matter code, so there was nothing to hold.

The workspace holds another paid plan term besides the invoice being refunded, so the operator's signed fee-refund command refuses and the refund is handled manually through support. No customer route returns this code; the fee refund exists only as that operator command.

The member rights update targeted the caller's own row and asked for a right the caller does not already hold. Self-revocation, a self-targeted monthly cap change and a self-grant of the reviewer right are still allowed; a self-grant of the billing right is allowed only while no member of the workspace holds it. Otherwise another admin has to grant the right.
The matter id named in the request does not exist in this workspace.
Another matter in this workspace already uses that matter code.
That matter is closed and cannot take new work.
This workspace has reached its configured matter limit.
The client id named in the request does not exist in this workspace.
Another client in this workspace already uses that client code.
That client is closed, so its matters cannot take new work either.
This workspace has reached its configured client limit.
The email_code sent to DELETE /api/me is wrong, expired, already used, or has had five wrong guesses. Request a new code with POST /api/me/deletion-code.
The caller has been rate limited. PAT-authenticated traffic carries a Retry-After header naming the wait in seconds; other rate-limited routes may not.
The account already has the maximum number of concurrent pipeline jobs in flight. Wait for one to finish before starting another.
The Insights provider's own capacity is temporarily exhausted. Retry the generation after a short delay.
The caller's IP has reached the daily limit for the anonymous preview endpoint. Retry after the daily window resets, or authenticate to use the ordinary upload flow instead.
The transcription provider returned an error or could not be reached. This is usually transient; retry after a delay.
The payment provider returned an error or could not be reached. This is usually transient; retry after a delay.
The transactional email provider could not be reached or refused the message. Not directly actionable by an API caller; the underlying action may still have succeeded.
An unexpected server-side failure occurred. Retry later; if it persists, it is a bug on the backend, not the request.

No longer emitted: no current route returns this code. It stays in the catalog, with its code, slug and status unchanged, for clients that may still key on it. It used to mean: The transcript's stored body could not be found or read where this action expected it. Treat as a transient storage fault and retry, or contact support if it persists.
